items.prose: Deal two cards from a full deck.
items.question: What is the chance both are hearts? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Condition on the first card being a heart.

byKey.replace: You squared $\tfrac14$. After one heart, only 12 of 51 are hearts.

explain.text: The first is a heart with chance $\tfrac14$; then 12 of the 51 left are. So $\tfrac{12}{204} = \tfrac1{17}$.

items.prose: An urn holds 4 red and 6 blue balls. You draw them all without replacement and without looking.
items.question: What is the chance the 9th ball is red?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Nothing has been seen, so use symmetry.

byKey.used: You assumed reds were used up. Nobody has seen the first eight.
byKey.blue: That is the chance it is blue.

explain.text: Drawing them all is a random order, so the 9th place is like the first: $\tfrac4{10}$.

items.prose: A screen flags 80% of faulty parts and 10% of good ones. 5% of parts are faulty.
items.question: A part is flagged. What is the chance it is faulty? Give four decimal places.

feedback.correct: Out of 1,000: 40 faulty and 95 good are flagged, so $\tfrac{40}{135} \approx 0.2963$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count flagged parts of each kind out of 1,000.

byKey.hit: You quoted the hit rate. Most flags come from the many good parts.
byKey.ratio: You divided 40 by 95. Divide by all 135 flagged.

explain.text: Out of 1,000 parts, 50 are faulty and 40 flagged; 950 are good and 95 flagged. So $\tfrac{40}{135} = \tfrac8{27}$.

items.prose: Fair £1 bets from £4, stopping at £0 or £12.
items.question: What is the expected number of bets?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the distances to the two ends.

byKey.sum: You added the distances. The duration multiplies them.
byKey.short: That is the shortest way down. Wins on the way add more bets.

explain.text: The fair duration is $k(N - k) = 32$. The chance of reaching £12 first is $\tfrac4{12} = \tfrac13$.

items.question: What is the chance the smaller face is at least 3? Give four decimal places.

feedback.correct: Both dice must show 3 or more: $(\tfrac46)^2 = \tfrac49$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. The smaller is at least 3 only if both are.

byKey.one: That is one die. Both must be at least 3.

items.prose: 50 ants sit at random points of a 1 m stick, facing random ways. They walk 1 m a minute and bounce on collision.
items.question: What is the expected time until the last falls, in minutes? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Treat the ants as ghosts and take the largest exit time.

byKey.one: That is the most it can take.

explain.text: Each ghost leaves at a uniform time; the last fall is the largest of 50, mean $\tfrac{50}{51}$.

items.prose: Turn a shuffled deck over one card at a time. There are 12 face cards: jacks, queens and kings.
items.question: At what position does the first face card appear, on average? Give four decimal places.

byKey.twelve: You split 52 into 12 parts. Twelve face cards make 13 gaps.
byKey.no-card: That counts the cards before it. Add one for the face card.

explain.text: Twelve face cards cut the 40 others into 13 gaps of mean $\tfrac{40}{13}$. The first face card is next, at $\tfrac{53}{13}$.

items.prose: Each £1 bet wins with chance 0.4. You start with £2 and stop at £0 or £5.
items.question: What is the chance of reaching £5? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Use $r = q/p = 1.5$ in $(1 - r^k)/(1 - r^N)$.

byKey.fair: That is the fair answer $\tfrac25$. The house edge cuts it hard.
byKey.flip: That is the chance of going broke.
byKey.inverse: You used $r = p/q$. The ratio is $q/p$.

explain.text: With $r = \tfrac{0.6}{0.4} = 1.5$, the chance is $\tfrac{1.25}{6.59375} \approx 0.19$. A 10-point edge against you halves the fair 0.4.

items.prose: A fault hits 1 in 1,000 machines. A check is 95% accurate on faulty and on sound machines alike. A machine fails the check.
items.question: Roughly how likely is it to be faulty?

options.why: You quoted the accuracy. Out of 100,000 machines, 95 faulty and 4,995 sound ones fail.
You split the failures evenly. Sound machines outnumber faulty ones 999 to 1.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count failures of each kind out of 100,000.

explain.text: Out of 100,000: 100 faulty with 95 failing, and 99,900 sound with 4,995 failing. So about $\tfrac{95}{5090} \approx 1.9\%$.

items.prose: Pólya’s urn from one red and one blue: draw, then return the ball with one more of its colour.
items.question: What is the chance the first three draws are red, red, blue? Give four decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Update the urn after each draw.

byKey.fixed: You kept every chance at $\tfrac12$. Each red adds a red, so the urn changes.
byKey.count: That is the chance of two reds in three draws, over all three orders.

explain.text: After R the urn holds 2 R and 1 B. After R, R it holds 3 R and 1 B, so blue has chance $\tfrac14$. The three paths with two reds give the uniform $\tfrac14$.
